street_smart.title: Your manager at work says 'do what I say or you're fired' and threatens to cut your job over something that isn't part of your duties or is clearly unfair. You're alone with them and they've raised their voice. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India, Oct 6: a Bengaluru warehouse manager was booked for allegedly threatening staff with 'learn Hindi or leave job'. Workplace threats are a real, reportable issue.
street_smart.situation: There are no witnesses in the room. The manager says nobody will believe you and that you can resign quietly if you don't like it.

choices.text: Argue back loudly and threaten to quit on the spot.
choices.feedback: An angry exchange gives them a counter-story ('insubordination') and you have nothing on record. Staying calm keeps the facts on your side.

choices.text: Stay calm, leave the conversation, then write down the date, time, exact words and who heard them, and send a factual email to HR to put it on record. If it was a threat, file a complaint with the police.
choices.feedback: A written, dated record converts a 'he said, she said' into evidence. In this week's case the manager was booked after staff complained, so complaints do get acted on.

choices.text: Quietly resign and sign whatever papers they hand you.
choices.feedback: A signed resignation or 'no dues' paper can cost you notice pay, dues and any claim later. Never sign anything under pressure.

choices.text: Post about it on social media with the manager's name and wait for the company to respond.
choices.feedback: Public posts without a formal complaint can expose you to defamation claims and give the company an excuse to act against you, while the actual threat stays unreported.

takeaways: Note date, time, words and witnesses right after the incident, and keep any messages.
Email HR a factual summary, and keep a copy of it for yourself.
Call 112 if you feel physically threatened, and never sign a resignation or settlement under pressure.

quiz.question: The Physics Nobel 2026 was awarded to Francis Halzen for discovering what?
quiz.why: Neutrinos are nearly massless particles that pass through matter almost untouched, which is why huge detectors are needed to catch them.

quiz.question: For how many days is Race Course Road in Bengaluru closed?
quiz.why: Closures like this usually come with alternate routes published by the traffic police, so check them before you travel.

quiz.question: Why are people checking 'Form 7' in the Bengaluru voter-list news?
options: To apply for a new voter ID
To object to or seek deletion of a name from the electoral roll
quiz.why: Form 6 is for adding a new voter. Forged Form-7 applications can get genuine voters deleted, which is why the roll is worth checking.
